title: Dedication
markdown:
# Dedication

![Visual reference from Dedication](../../assets/figures/page-0003-visual.webp)

The Maine EMS Prehospital Treatment Protocols are dedicated to Maine's EMS clinicians, both past and present, as well as the numerous physicians, PAs, NPs, nurses and other medical personnel who have provided their time and guidance over the years to make the development of these protocols possible. This document reflects the planned review, which occurs every two years, by the Medical Direction and Practices Board. The MDPB attempts to combine the best available evidence from the current literature and medical consensus together to produce protocols that will enhance prehospital care in the State of Maine.

Many individuals have spearheaded the effort for this work to become a reality. Although there are too many to mention individually, it is important to realize the common commitment shared to empower a continuously improving system where those citizens who need emergency medical assistance receive the best care possible.

For those of you reading this document, please keep in mind the great commitment and sacrifice that Maine EMS clinicians make daily in the course of providing superlative prehospital care. Their work is physically, emotionally, and mentally stressful, yet 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, these individuals provide care with the skill and compassion that promises the best prehospital care for all of the citizens of Maine. What you do matters and we thank you.

The MDPB would like to particularly recognize the efforts of two former MDPB members and dedicate the 2025 Maine EMS Protocols to these individuals. First, Dr. Kate Zimmerman, for her service initially as the Region 1 Medical Director then as the Associate State Medical Director. Her efforts have been instrumental to this Maine EMS Protocol update as well as prior updates. The MDPB is grateful for her leadership, dedication, and engagement with the Maine EMS system. Second, Dr. Kevin Kendall, who served as the Maine ACEP Representative to the MDPB, and whose passion for prehospital care and engagement in the Maine EMS system acts as a model for subsequent Maine EMS physicians.
